subject: Clarify streaming guarantees vs fallback + throughput expectations
messages:
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearwave.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming SLA expectations for pilot – details attached

Hi Neha / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we scope the pilot, security and latency guarantees are top of mind for our clinical UX team. Attached is a short spreadsheet with our expected targets. Can you confirm Redwood can meet these for a streaming endpoint? Specific asks:

- Time-to-first-token (median): <= 200ms for typical 1–2 token prefix on p8-p10 questions
- Sustained token emission: 60–80 tokens/sec per connection for 8k sequence workloads
- Availability: 99.9% for the streaming endpoint in us-west region, with documented fallback behavior if the stream degrades

We are open to hybrid approaches but need concrete fallback guarantees (how quickly a polled endpoint will return completion; billing implications if fallback occurs). Procurement wants this in writing to proceed.

Attached: clearwave-requirements.xlsx

Thanks,
Tom Liu
Head of Engineering, ClearWave Health
Tom.Liu@clearwave.ai

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearwave.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA expectations for pilot – details attached

Tom — thanks for the clear list. I pulled our SRE and product folks into the thread (Karthik) so we can give you a concrete proposal. Quick answers up front:

- Baseline hosted streaming: target median TTFT for the model family you saw is 120–220ms depending on sequence length and upstream tokenization. We typically publish a median around 150ms on the catalog for the model variant we demoed.
- Sustained emit rate: for a single connection we can sustain ~70 tokens/sec on p8-class instances for 8k-ish contexts with KV cache and batching enabled; with dedicated pools that number can be increased.
- Availability: we operate 99.95% platform uptime for hosted endpoints; specific live-stream availability for a given region is tracked per-deployment.

Two asks from our side so we align:
1) Can you confirm the percent of requests that must be streaming vs acceptable to fall back to polled (sync) behavior?
2) For billing: do you expect us to bill at the streaming rate during fallback or at the polled endpoint rate?

We can propose a limited carveout for the pilot: a hybrid SLA that sets an actionable TTFT target (median <= 220ms) with a documented automatic fallback to a polled endpoint if the stream drops below a detection threshold for longer than 3s. During fallback the client will receive a single completion with expected latency window (typically 400–1200ms depending on prompt). We can provide a credit if fallback frequency exceeds X/month during the pilot.

I'll let Karthik add the technical constraints and a wording you can include in procurement. Attaching a draft SLO (slo-draft-redwood-v1.docx).

—Neha 
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearwave.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA expectations for pilot – details attached

Tom — sliced technical response below (keeping it pragmatic for procurement):

1) Why TTFT varies: TTFT depends on queueing in our continuous-batching fabric, model cold-starts for KV cache misses, and the host GPU scheduling. For the model you evaluated, median TTFT is 150ms for short prompts under nominal load; p99 can spike above 400ms under heavy multi-tenant contention.

2) Proposed pilot SLO (explicit wording you can paste):
   - "For the pilot, Redwood will target median time-to-first-token (TTFT) <= 220ms for streaming endpoints serving the ClearWave pilot in us-west, over a 30-day rolling window."
   - "If sustained per-connection emit rate falls below 20 tokens/sec for a period > 3s due to resource contention or preemption, Redwood will automatically trigger a deterministic failover to a compatible polled endpoint. The polled endpoint will return a completion response with an expected latency between 400–1200ms depending on sequence length. Failovers will be logged and visible in the Console; if failovers exceed 2% of requests in a 30-day window, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 10% of the monthly usage for affected endpoints."
   - "Availability for the streaming surface will be measured via successful initial handshake + TTFT observed; platform uptime SLA remains 99.95% for the account. Specific streaming availability metrics will be included in the pilot addendum."

3) Billing during fallback: we propose billing at the streaming rate for the request if the server started streaming TTL (i.e., partial tokens emitted), otherwise charge the polled rate. For transparency we will show the billing line items per-request in Console export.

4) Testing and validation: we can provide a canary plan (5% traffic, synthetic load) and a short test harness you can run to validate TTFT and token/sec. Expect a 48–72 hour window to run representative tests.

Marissa — flagging for legal to vet the credit wording and any required indemnities for clinical throughput.

—Karthik (Product / SRE liaison)

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearwave.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA expectations for pilot – details attached

Thanks — this is helpful and closer to what procurement needs. A few clarifications before we loop legal: 

- The 220ms median TTFT is acceptable for the pilot, but procurement is pushing for a p95 commitment as well. Would you be able to offer p95 <= 400ms for the pilot window?
- The fallback credit: can you make the trigger more action-oriented (e.g., credit if failovers > 1% in a 30-day window) — ClearWave runs high-volume clinical triage at peak hours and 2% is risky for us.
- We will run the canary; procurement attached our standard form (procurement-form.pdf). Please route to finance/legal with your comments.

If we can get p95 <= 400ms and reduce the failover threshold to 1% we should be able to start the PO process.

—Tom

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@clearwave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA expectations for pilot – details attached

Tom — appreciate the specificity. Proposed compromise and next steps: 

- Redwood accepts the pilot SLO set to median TTFT <= 220ms and p95 TTFT <= 420ms for the 30-day pilot window (we reserve the right to document known caveats re: extreme load/cold starts in the Schedule).
- We will adjust the credit trigger to failovers > 1% in a 30-day window. If that threshold is exceeded Redwood will issue a pro-rated credit equal to 15% of usage for the impacted endpoints for that billing month.
- Billing clarification: if the server begins emitting tokens we will bill at the streaming unit rate; if a request is fully served by the polled fallback we will bill at the polled rate. All fallback events will be exportable from Console for reconciliation.
- Action items:
   1) Legal/Finance — please review the proposed credit language and the pilot SLA wording attached (slo-draft-redwood-v1.docx).
   2) SRE/Eng — we will schedule the canary: suggested window Wed–Thu (48 hours), RPS and synthetic prompt list to be provided.
   3) Procurement — we received your form; we will return a redline by EOD Wed.

If that works I'll move this to a short redline with Marissa and get the DocuSign envelope queued (link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ENVELOPE-12345).

Thanks — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
